summary.motive: Create a natural rub with two shallow crossers and let each receiver convert off the defender's leverage rather than a fixed break point.
summary.whyItWorks: Crossers force man defenders to exchange or collide through traffic, and the read-route rules guarantee one receiver is always working away from his coverage.
summary.failureMode: Defenders pass off the crossers cleanly pre-snap, or a blitz disrupts the timing before the mesh point develops.

beats.title: 1. The Vertical Stems Sell Out
beats.text: Both crossers release on pure vertical stems while X and Y push the corners deep, convincing the safeties that this is a four-vertical shot.

beats.title: 2. The Mesh Point
beats.text: The crossers converge at midfield within a yard of each other. Man defenders must either exchange or collide, and the linebackers cannot communicate fast enough.

beats.title: 3. Reading the Leverage
beats.text: The chase-over forces M to settle into the soft hole between the linebacker levels, while Z feels trail leverage and speeds up, climbing away from SAM.

beats.title: 4. The Window Throw
beats.text: The quarterback hits Z climbing up the far seam in front of a free safety whose eyes never left the corner route.

relations.tell: The crossers never stop until they feel a defender's leverage — a called mesh with set breaks settles at the same spot every snap regardless of coverage.
